title: Phantom same-pack version edges make a lock resource permanently un-removable
description:
From TASK-200's gating review (MEDIUM-1), demonstrated empirically by the reviewer rather than reasoned about.

**The defect.** Owner strings are `pack-id@version` (e.g. `watch@2.0.0`, composed at `src/pack-orchestrator.js:73`). TASK-200 changed `executeInstall` to preserve-and-union owner edges instead of resetting them — correctly, because the reset was dropping *sibling packs'* edges and breaking `executeRemove`'s "a still-owned resource is never deleted" guarantee.

But nothing drops a pack's **own stale version-suffixed edge** when that pack bumps its descriptor version while still wanting the same resource. The old buggy reset cleaned these up incidentally; preserve-and-union does not.

**Reviewer's probe, reproduced in a sandbox:** prior owners `["design-power@0.1.0","watch@1.0.0"]`; a replace executed by `watch@2.0.0` yields `["design-power@0.1.0","watch@1.0.0","watch@2.0.0"]`. After **both** `watch@2.0.0` and `design-power@0.1.0` remove, the entry survives with `["watch@1.0.0"]` and the live directory is still on disk. No reconciler flow can ever clear it: `dropOwner` is an exact-string match and nothing anywhere parses a pack-id out of `pack-id@version`.

**Why it was right to land TASK-200 anyway, and why this still needs closing.** The failure direction is *retention*, which a human can recover with a manual lock edit. The alternative the old code implemented was *deletion of a sibling's working skill*, which is unrecoverable. And `plan()`'s removal candidacy already requires owners-empty (`src/pack-reconcile.js:231-234`), so no end-to-end reconcile flow reaches the stranding today — it bites only direct `applyPlan` callers.

But phantom edges **accumulate monotonically** with every version-bump-plus-re-materialize, and each one quietly hollows out `executeRemove`'s contract for any future caller. Retention that can never be cleared is a slow leak, not a safe default.

**Suggested fix (the reviewer's, and it looks right).** During the union, drop prior edges whose pack-id matches the current owner's pack-id but whose version differs. Owner strings are `${descriptor.id}@${descriptor.version}`, so a last-`@` split is well-defined. Note that no pack-id parsing exists anywhere in the codebase today — introducing it is a real (if small) new concept, so keep it in one place and name it.

**Also fold in the TASK-200 LOW while in this file:** the decision comment at `src/pack-apply.js:449-450` claims `dropOwner`/`isOrphaned` are "the only other readers of `owners[]`", but `plan()` also reads it via an inlined owners-empty check (`src/pack-reconcile.js:231-232`) and `assimilateSkill` writes it (`src/assimilate.js:593`). The conclusion holds; the survey does not.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first reproduces the strand: a pack bumps its descriptor version, re-materializes a resource, then every owning pack removes - and the lock entry plus live directory survive with a phantom pack@old-version edge. Capture the red-run output verbatim.
Same-pack stale-version edges no longer accumulate: after a version-bumped re-materialize, the resource carries exactly one edge for that pack, and sibling packs' edges are untouched.
A sensor exists for the condition itself - a resource carrying two edges with the same pack-id and different versions - so a regression is caught mechanically rather than by inspection.

The cross-pack guarantee TASK-200 established does not regress: after a replace by pack B, a resource still owned by pack A is still not removable as an orphan. Re-run TASK-200's own AC3 spec as part of the gate.

Pack-id parsing is introduced in exactly one named place with its assumption stated (owner strings are ${descriptor.id}@${descriptor.version}), and what happens to a malformed owner string is decided rather than left implicit.
The TASK-200 LOW is fixed in passing: src/pack-apply.js's decision comment correctly names every reader and writer of owners[], including plan()'s inlined check and assimilateSkill's write.
npm run test:all is green; dist/pack-ctl.cjs rebuilt and committed if bundled source changes, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
**APPROVE** — range `09455c8..cb04491`, FULL depth, tier `tdd`. **0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM (process) / 5 LOW.**

**Gate:** `test:since -- 09455c8` 8 files / 135 passed, no zero-selection marker ⬛ `npm test` 87 files / 1178 passed, 2 skipped ⬛ `test:all` **188 passed | 1 skipped (189 files), 2192 passed | 4 skipped, 0 failed**, 83.69s — exactly baseline 2171 + the 21 new tests ⬛ named e2e expanded to 8 files / 122 passed ⬛ `dist-parity` all 8 bundles green ⬛ `check:calibration` clean.

## AC1 — red state reproduced INDEPENDENTLY, not taken on faith

The hand-off's red run was 15 `is not a function` failures plus 3 real assertion failures; the former prove nothing. So the reviewer rebuilt both revisions into a scratchpad sandbox (`git archive` of each rev, repo never mutated) and drove the committed AC1/AC2 scenarios through the **real `applyPlan`** of each:

```
=========== PRE-FIX (09455c8) ===========
  owners after version-bumped replace : ["design-power@0.1.0","watch@1.0.0","watch@2.0.0"]
  entry after BOTH owners removed     : ["watch@1.0.0"]
  live dir still on disk              : true
  AC1 assertions -> FAIL
=========== POST-FIX (cb04491) ===========
  owners after version-bumped replace : ["design-power@0.1.0","watch@2.0.0"]
  entry after BOTH owners removed     : undefined (removed)
  live dir still on disk              : false
  AC1 assertions -> PASS
```

The strand is genuine and the load-bearing assertions fail for the right reason against pre-fix source. Tests-first invariant proven.

## AC3 sensor — vacuity audit (the flagged highest risk), three checks, all clear

- **Fail-on-stub is real.** Two assertions demand non-empty output (`tests/integrations-lock.spec.js:355` and `:383`). Stubbing `findDuplicatePackIdOwners → []` fails exactly those two and nothing else.
- **Fires on real data.** The repo's actual `integrations.lock.json` with one duplicate injected → `[{"id":"skill:watch","packIds":["watch"]}]`. Clean file → `[]`.
- **Not the TASK-184 empty-checked-set class.** The checked set is `Object.entries(lock.resources)` = 2 real resources, not an empty set derived from a success-only fixture. A deleted/renamed lockfile makes the spec throw ENOENT — loud, the correct direction. `integrations.lock.json` is git-tracked, so this is not a machine-local artifact that would break a fresh clone.

## AC5 — malformed-owner contract probed directly

```
""  -> null    "@"  -> null    "@@" -> null    "a@" -> null    "@1.0.0" -> null    "  " -> null
"a@b@1.0.0" -> {packId:"a@b", version:"1.0.0"}      "a@@1.0.0" -> {packId:"a@", version:"1.0.0"}
```
Every documented case matches the stated contract. All three call sites honour `null` as "leave it alone" with no guessed fallback (`src/integrations-lock.js:212`, `:215`, `:242`).

**Can "leave it alone" itself strand?** Chased and answered no. The original defect made an edge unreachable because a *version bump* changed the string. A malformed owner has no version component to bump — its string is stable, so the pack that wrote it can always drop it with the identical string. The default composition path cannot produce one either (`state/pack-descriptor.schema.json` requires `id` and `version` at `minLength: 1`); a malformed edge is reachable only via an explicitly-passed `opts.owner`, which the same caller can drop exactly. Retention is also the recoverable direction, consistent with the ticket's own reasoning.

Incidental improvement confirmed: `owners:` is now a fresh array rather than the pre-fix alias of `priorEntry.owners`.

## AC4 / AC6 / scope

- **AC4:** TASK-200's own AC3 spec re-run in isolation — 3 passed / 23 skipped. No regression.
- **AC6 survey verified by the reviewer's OWN grep**, not the developer's list: `owners` appears in `src/integrations-lock.js`, `src/pack-apply.js`, `src/pack-reconcile.js:231-232`, `src/assimilate.js:593` and `:611`; `bin/` has zero matches. The survey at `src/pack-apply.js:455-469` names all of them at function granularity.
- **Scope boundary respected:** `src/assimilate.js` untouched — the TASK-203 sibling defect is only *named*, not fixed.
- **No corruption from the disclosed throwaway-script incident:** `src/integrations-lock.js` ends cleanly at line 274, imports and executes under node, diff contains no stray artifact, `git status` shows no leftover script.

## Findings

**MEDIUM (process, hand-off).** Only three of five Pre-hand-off checklist items had stated outcomes in the reviewer's inputs. All three unstated ones were independently verified clean.

**LOW-1** `tests/integrations-lock.spec.js:406-413` — the permanent live-repo sensor cannot fire against today's data (2 resources, 1 owner each), so the ≥2-same-pack-id condition is structurally unreachable right now. Non-vacuous in mechanism, but its present value is **purely prospective** — the actual write-path regression coverage is carried by the three e2e tests. Worth knowing so nobody mistakes its green for evidence about the write path.

**LOW-2 (the interesting one)** `src/integrations-lock.js:165` — the doc comment says a *version* containing `@` "is not a documented shape at all", but nothing enforces it: the descriptor schema only requires `version` `minLength: 1` ("semver-exact recommended, not enforced here"). A version like `1.0@beta` bumped to `2.0@beta` splits to pack-ids `watch@1.0` vs `watch@2.0`, so `dropStaleSameOwnerEdges` would **not** drop the stale edge — the exact strand recurs, and the AC3 sensor is blind to it for the same reason. Likelihood essentially nil (no semver contains `@`) and the assumption IS stated, so AC5 is satisfied. Suggested fix: `"pattern": "^[^@]+$"` on `version` in `state/pack-descriptor.schema.json`.

**LOW-3** `tests/integrations-lock.spec.js:387` — mild new-test-budget redundancy; the same negative case is covered at `:369` and again by the live-repo sensor. The other 20 new tests each encode a distinct AC branch or contract edge and are within budget.

**LOW-4** `src/pack-apply.js:464` — the survey names `assimilateSkill` as a writer but not its accompanying read at `src/assimilate.js:611`. Same function, conclusion unaffected.

**LOW-5 (process, Orchestrator-side)** the ticket was still `in_progress` when the reviewer was spawned; workflow step 6 requires `transition_status` to `in_review` first.

## Sweep

Unspecced path, vacuous sensor, stale dist, parity drift, calibration laundering — all clear. Tier-audit clear: `tdd` is correct for state-mutation logic and the red-run evidence was independently reproduced. Minimalism clear: `findLockResourcesWithDuplicatePackIdOwners` has a single caller (its spec), but that is rung-1 Necessity (AC3) and mirrors `src/graph-freshness.js#findDoneTicketsMissingGraphNodes`, likewise called only from its spec.

**Verdict: APPROVE.**

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**CLOSED on a green independent review.** Review depth **FULL**; rubric inputs: 482 changed lines (475 added / 7 removed) across 5 files — over the 150 threshold — AND the diff touches packaging/dist (`dist/pack-ctl.cjs`) plus core `tdd`-tier logic (`src/pack-apply.js`, `src/integrations-lock.js`). Any one input alone forces FULL.

Commit `cb04491`. Tier `tdd`, single developer spawn, single commit; the captured red-run evidence is the tests-first proof and the reviewer **independently reproduced the pre-fix strand** in a `git archive` sandbox rather than accepting the hand-off's red run — correctly, since 15 of the 21 reported red failures were `is not a function` and prove nothing on their own.

## What landed

`parseOwnerEdge` in `src/integrations-lock.js` is the single named home for pack-id parsing (AC5) — a genuinely new concept in this codebase, deliberately placed alongside `addOwner`/`dropOwner`/`isOrphaned`. Its assumption (`${descriptor.id}@${descriptor.version}`, last-`@` split) is documented, and the **malformed case is decided, not implicit**: no `@`, empty id, or empty version all return `null`, and every call site treats `null` as "cannot be attributed, leave it alone" — never a guessed fallback. `dropStaleSameOwnerEdges` then removes only a prior edge with the same packId and a different version, wired into `executeInstall` just before `addOwner`.

The reviewer chased the obvious follow-up question — **can "leave it alone" itself strand?** — and answered no with a real argument: the original defect made an edge unreachable because a *version bump* changed the string; a malformed owner has no version component to bump, so its string is stable and the pack that wrote it can always drop it with the identical string. The default composition path cannot produce one either. That is the right shape of answer for a fail-safe default.

## Residual accepted, recorded rather than fixed (LOW-2)

`src/integrations-lock.js:165` claims a *version* containing `@` "is not a documented shape at all", but nothing enforces it — `state/pack-descriptor.schema.json` only requires `version` at `minLength: 1`, explicitly noting semver is "recommended, not enforced here". A version like `1.0@beta` bumped to `2.0@beta` splits to pack-ids `watch@1.0` vs `watch@2.0`, so the stale edge would **not** be dropped and this exact strand recurs — with the AC3 sensor blind to it for the same reason.

**Accepted, not fixed here.** Likelihood is essentially nil (no semver contains `@`), the assumption IS stated in code so AC5 is satisfied, and tightening the descriptor schema is a schema change that belongs in its own ticket rather than being smuggled into this one. The one-line fix, if it is ever wanted, is `"pattern": "^[^@]+$"` on `version` in `state/pack-descriptor.schema.json`.

## LOW-1 is worth remembering, because it is an honesty point about our own sensor

The AC3 live-repo sensor (`tests/integrations-lock.spec.js:406-413`) is non-vacuous in **mechanism** — proven three ways: fail-on-stub fails exactly the two non-empty assertions; it fires on the real lockfile with a duplicate injected; and its checked set is 2 real resources, not the TASK-184 empty-checked-set class. But it **cannot fire against today's data**, because `integrations.lock.json` holds 2 resources with exactly 1 owner each, making the ≥2-same-pack-id condition structurally unreachable right now.

So its value is **purely prospective**. The actual write-path regression coverage is carried by the three e2e tests, not by this sensor. Recording that explicitly so nobody later mistakes its green for evidence about the write path — which is precisely the inference this repo's Empty-result contract exists to prevent.

## Other findings, all accepted without rework

- **MEDIUM (process)** — only three of five pre-hand-off checklist items had stated outcomes in the reviewer's inputs. **DISCHARGED:** the raw hand-off did carry all five; items 4 (parity, `n/a` — no parity-copy files touched) and 5 (calibration, `n/a` — no markers carried forward) were stated and the briefing summarized rather than relayed them. The reviewer independently verified all three unstated ones clean anyway.
- **LOW-3** mild new-test-budget redundancy at `tests/integrations-lock.spec.js:387`; the other 20 of 21 new tests each encode a distinct AC branch or contract edge and are within budget.
- **LOW-4** the AC6 survey names `assimilateSkill` as a writer but not its read at `src/assimilate.js:611`. Same function, conclusion unaffected.
- **LOW-5 (mine)** — **a real Orchestrator process error, acknowledged.** The ticket was still `in_progress` when the reviewer was spawned; workflow step 6 requires `transition_status` to `in_review` **first**, since `done` is reachable only from `in_review` and that transition is the one step in the documented convention implying a review occurred. Corrected before this close. TASK-198 was done correctly earlier in the same session, so this was a slip, not a misunderstanding of the rule.

## Scope boundary held

`src/assimilate.js` was left untouched — its sibling `owners: []`-then-re-add clobber is **TASK-203**, which follows next and must reuse `parseOwnerEdge` rather than inventing a second implementation of the same invariant. The AC6 comment now names it as the known outstanding writer.

`dist/pack-ctl.cjs` was rebuilt and committed; `dist-parity` byte-matches all 8 bundles. The disclosed throwaway-script incident during the non-vacuity proof left nothing corrupt — the committed file parses, executes, and the diff carries no stray artifact.
